name: Smyth
description: Three Michelin stars. Hyper-seasonal farm-driven tasting menu from John and Karen Shields. Kelp tarts with English pea butter, foie gras doughnuts. The pinnacle.
must_try: Full tasting menu — changes with what the farm sends

name: Alinea
description: Two Michelin stars. Grant Achatz's theatrical, immersive tasting menu. The edible helium balloon and tabletop dessert presentations are legendary.
must_try: The full tasting — there is no à la carte

name: Ever
description: Two Michelin stars. Curtis Duffy's wood-fire-driven tasting menu in Fulton Market. Pristine ingredients, elemental cooking.

name: Kasama
description: Two Michelin stars. Tim Flores and Genie Kwon's Filipino tasting menu — a watershed moment for the cuisine globally. Adobo of mussels, mais con yelo with sweet corn semifreddo.
must_try: Evening tasting menu (daytime is a bakery/brunch counter)

name: Oriole
description: Two Michelin stars in an unmarked West Loop alley. Noah Sandoval's Japanese-influenced tasting menu. Intimate, no-signage speakeasy entrance.

name: Indienne
description: One Michelin star. 2026 Banchet Award Restaurant of the Year. Indian-French tasting menus for omnivores, vegans, and pescatarians. Chef Sujan Sarkar.

name: Boka
description: One Michelin star in Lincoln Park. Seasonal American tasting menu in a gorgeous townhouse setting.

name: Elske
description: One Michelin star. David and Anna Posey's Scandinavian-Midwestern tasting menu. The pastry program is extraordinary.
must_try: Tasting menu with optional wine pairing

name: Schwa
description: One Michelin star. BYOB, cash-only, no-reservations-system chaos. Michael Carlson's punk-rock fine dining in Wicker Park. Legendary and unpredictable.
must_try: Whatever the kitchen sends — there's no menu
hours: Irregular — call or check social media

name: Topolobampo
description: One Michelin star. Rick Bayless's upscale Mexican fine dining. Decades-deep mastery of regional Mexican cuisine.

name: El Ideas
description: One Michelin star since 2013. Chef Foss hosts a dinner party for 20 every night. BYOB. Douglas Park. Under-the-radar gem that's maintained its star for 13 years.
must_try: Full tasting — BYOB your best bottle

name: Feld
description: One Michelin star plus Green Star for sustainability. Chef Jacob Potashnick sources everything within a 4-hour radius. New wave Chicago fine dining.

name: Moody Tongue
description: One Michelin star. Culinary brewery in the South Loop — tasting menu paired with their own brewed beers. Unique concept.

name: Sepia
description: One Michelin star. Sophisticated American cuisine in a gorgeous Art Nouveau space. West Loop stalwart.

name: Next
description: One Michelin star. Grant Achatz's concept restaurant — the menu theme changes entirely every few months. Tickets sold in advance like a show.

name: Mako
description: One Michelin star. Omakase-style Japanese tasting menu in the West Loop.

name: Galit
description: One Michelin star. Middle Eastern fine dining in Lincoln Park. Bold, fire-driven cooking. Chef Zachary Engel.

name: Cariño
description: One Michelin star. Elevated Mexican in Uptown. Small, intimate, deeply personal cooking.

name: Esmé
description: One Michelin star. Contemporary fine dining in Lincoln Park. Playful, artistic presentations.

name: Atelier
description: One Michelin star in Lincoln Square. American tasting menu in a neighborhood setting.

name: Girl & the Goat
description: Stephanie Izard's flagship. Bold globally-inspired shared plates. Bib Gourmand. Still one of the hardest reservations in town.
must_try: Goat empanadas, wood-oven roasted pig face

name: Giant
description: Bib Gourmand. Jason Vincent's Logan Square neighborhood gem. Seasonal American with serious technique and zero pretension.

name: Longman & Eagle
description: Bib Gourmand. Logan Square gastropub with rooms upstairs. Whiskey list is insane. Brunch is legendary.
must_try: Wild boar sloppy joe, whiskey flight

name: Lula Cafe
description: Bib Gourmand. Logan Square institution since 1999. Farm-to-table before it was a movement. Monday night prix fixe is legendary.

name: The Publican
description: Beer-hall-meets-fine-dining in Fulton Market. Pork, oysters, one of the best beer lists in the Midwest.
must_try: Pork rinds, frites with duck fat

name: Daisies
description: Bib Gourmand. Logan Square pasta gem. Handmade pasta, creative cocktails, accessible prices.
must_try: Whatever fresh pasta is on the menu

name: Frontera Grill
description: Bib Gourmand. Rick Bayless's original. Regional Mexican with market-driven ingredients. More casual sister to Topolobampo.

name: HaiSous Vietnamese Kitchen
description: Bib Gourmand. Pilsen Vietnamese. The whole fish and the pho are transcendent. One of the most beloved restaurants in the city.

name: Virtue
description: Bib Gourmand. James Beard Award-winning Erick Williams. Elevated Southern heritage cooking in Hyde Park. Culture of hospitality.

name: Superkhana International
description: Bib Gourmand. Logan Square Indian with a punk sensibility. Bold flavors, communal energy, BYOB.

name: Birrieria Zaragoza
description: Bib Gourmand. James Beard Award-winning birria. The goat consommé and tacos are a pilgrimage.

name: Mi Tocaya Antojeria
description: Bib Gourmand. Diana Dávila's modern Mexican in Logan Square. Elevated antojitos with deep cultural roots.

name: Mott St.
description: Bib Gourmand. Wicker Park fusion — Asian street food meets Midwestern soul. Late-night energy.

name: Pleasant House Pub
description: Bib Gourmand. British-style savory pies in Pilsen. The Royal Pie (steak and ale) is the standard.

name: Ciccio Mio
description: Bib Gourmand. Intimate River North Italian. Yelp Top 100 nationally. Handmade pasta in a room that feels like nonna's kitchen.
must_try: Fresh pasta — whatever the special is

name: Sifr
description: Bib Gourmand. Wood-fired Middle Eastern in River North. The $60 four-course tasting menu is the biggest steal in Chicago dining.

name: Perilla
description: Bib Gourmand. Korean in the West Loop. Modern takes on Korean classics.

name: Taqueria Chingón
description: Bib Gourmand. Mexico City street food elevated — duck carnitas and al pastor carved from the trompo onto griddled tortillas.

name: Lou Malnati's Pizzeria
description: The deep-dish standard. Buttery crust, chunky tomato sauce, sausage patty that covers the whole pie.

name: Pequod's Pizza
description: Caramelized cheese crust deep dish that converts thin-crust loyalists. The crunchy blackened cheese edge is the move.
must_try: Pan pizza with sausage — ask for extra crispy

name: Giordano's
description: Stuffed deep-dish — thicker than Lou's, more cheese, tourist-heavy. Fine but not the local move.

name: Pizzeria Uno
description: Where deep-dish was literally invented in 1943. The original location. More historic landmark than best-in-class pizza.
must_try: Original deep dish in the room where it started

name: Vito & Nick's
description: The platonic ideal of tavern-style pizza. Cracker-thin crust, cut in squares, aggressively unpretentious. Ashburn. Since 1946.

name: Pat's Pizza
description: Lincoln Park tavern-style since 1950. Ultra-thin crust that shatters. What actual Chicagoans eat daily.

name: Al's #1 Italian Beef
description: The original Italian beef since 1938. Stand-up counter, no frills, invented a food category.
must_try: Italian beef combo — dipped, hot peppers

name: Portillo's
description: Chicago fast food royalty. Italian beef, Chicago dogs, and a chocolate cake shake that has no business being that good.
must_try: Italian beef, dipped, with hot giardiniera

name: Johnnie's Beef
address: 7500 W North Ave, Elmwood Park, IL 60707
description: Suburban Italian beef legend. Stand-up only, no seats. The beef drips. Worth the drive from the city.

name: Mr. Beef
description: River North Italian beef counter. Got famous from The Bear TV show. The real deal — Jay Leno used to fly these in.
must_try: Italian beef, sweet and hot peppers

name: Superdawg Drive-In
description: Iconic drive-in since 1948. Giant hot dog statues on the roof. Classic Chicago dog with carhop service.

name: Gene & Jude's
address: 2720 N River Rd, River Grove, IL 60171
description: The most Chicago hot dog stand that exists. No ketchup, no seats, no nonsense. Depression Dog with fries dumped on top.
must_try: Depression Dog with fries on top

name: Jim's Original
description: Maxwell Street stand since 1939. Polish sausage and hot dogs. Open-air, charcoal-grilled, served with grilled onions and sport peppers.
must_try: Maxwell Street Polish with grilled onions

name: Byron's Hot Dogs
address: 1017 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60613
description: Classic Chicago dog stand near Wrigley. Everything dragged through the garden. No ketchup.

name: Bavette's Bar & Boeuf
description: Moody jazz-age steakhouse in River North. Dark leather, candlelight, live music. The shrimp DeJonghe is the best appetizer in the city.

name: Gibsons Bar & Steakhouse
description: The quintessential Chicago power steakhouse since 1989. Enormous cuts, legendary bar scene.

name: Chicago Cut Steakhouse
description: River-facing steakhouse with a gorgeous patio. The dry-aged prime is the focus. Power lunch crowd.

name: Maple & Ash
description: Gold Coast steakhouse where the 'I Don't Give a F*@k' menu lets the kitchen choose for you. Bold, theatrical.
must_try: The IDGAF menu — let the kitchen decide

name: Swift & Sons
description: Fulton Market steakhouse from the Boka group. Whole-animal butchery program, craft cocktails, old-Chicago vibes.

name: RPM Italian
description: River North Italian from the Lettuce Entertain You/RPM group. Scene-y, loud, great pasta. Celebrity sightings.
must_try: Cacio e pepe, short rib ravioli

name: Gene & Georgetti
description: Chicago's oldest steakhouse, since 1941. Old-school Italian-American steakhouse beneath the L tracks. Sinatra ate here.

name: Joe's Seafood, Prime Steak & Stone Crab
description: Miami import on the Mag Mile. Stone crab claws flown from Florida, prime steaks.
must_try: Stone crab claws with mustard sauce

name: Shaw's Crab House
description: River North seafood institution. Raw bar, classic preparations, great oyster happy hour.
must_try: Oyster happy hour at the raw bar

name: Au Cheval
description: The cheeseburger that launched a thousand hour-long waits. Double with fried egg. Fulton Market.

name: Big Star
description: Wicker Park taco joint with honky-tonk soul. Carnitas tacos, frozen margaritas, best patio energy in the city.

name: Monteverde
description: Sarah Grueneberg's West Loop pasta temple. The cacio e pepe tortelloni is iconic. Every pasta is made in-house.

name: Wildberry Pancakes and Cafe
description: Best brunch downtown. Line is real but moves fast. Berry bliss pancakes and signature skillets.

name: Lou Mitchell's
description: Near Union Station since 1923. Thick-cut French toast, double-yolk eggs. They hand you donut holes while you wait.
must_try: French toast, donut holes in line

name: Yolk
description: Multi-location brunch with creative egg dishes, healthy bowls, specialty juices. Solid and consistent.

name: Big Jones
description: Andersonville Southern brunch that changes lives. Heritage grain biscuits, shrimp and grits. Chef Paul Fehribach.
must_try: Southern brunch — biscuits, shrimp and grits

name: MingHin Cuisine
description: Chinatown's most popular dim sum. Modern, spacious, good cart service. Always packed on weekends.
must_try: Dim sum — har gow, siu mai, egg tarts

name: Lao Sze Chuan
description: Chinatown Sichuan that defines authentic and numbing. Tony Hu's flagship. The dry chili chicken is legend.

name: Carnitas Don Pedro
description: Pilsen slow-cooked pork institution on 18th Street. Carnitas by the pound with tortillas and salsa.

name: Ghareeb Nawaz
description: Devon Ave Pakistani/Indian. High-volume, insanely cheap, exceptionally spiced. Open late. Green chili chicken.

name: Pearl's Place
description: Bronzeville classic Southern fine dining. Sunday brunch is a community institution. White tablecloths, real hospitality.

name: Luella's Southern Kitchen
description: Lincoln Square scratch-made Southern using Midwestern farm products. Fried chicken and biscuits.

name: Atsumeru
description: 2026 opening. Nordic-Japanese tasting menu, 8 seats, seafood-forward. Chef Devin Denzer. 10-12 course menu.

name: Monster Ramen
description: 2025 opening. Chef Katie Dong's in-house Noodle Lab producing fresh organic noodles daily. Wagyu Miso ramen is the move.
must_try: The Monster — wagyu rib roast, beef jam, soft-boiled egg

name: Petit Pomeroy
address: One Chicago, River North, Chicago, IL 60611
description: 2026 opening. Parisian bistro downtown from the acclaimed Winnetka team. Classic French fare, extensive Burgundy list.

name: Void
description: 2025 opening. Moody Italian in Avondale — vintage charm, dive bar vibes, creative pasta. The spaghetti uh-os went viral.

name: Dimmi Dimmi
description: 2025 opening. Modern neighborhood Italian-American. Ex-Carbone chef. Red-sauce favorites with Chicago giardiniera twist.

name: Tre Dita
description: 2025 opening. Hand-rolled pasta with flour from Italy. The hottest Italian opening — hype is backed up.

name: Lao Der
description: Chicago's first sit-down Lao restaurant in years. Khao piek sen noodle soup stops tables mid-conversation. BYOB.

name: Elia
description: 2025 opening. Turkish kebabs, hot mezes, fresh pita. Mediterranean bar and lounge energy.

name: Kingston Mines
description: Chicago's premier blues club since 1968. Two stages, live music seven nights, no breaks between sets. 4AM license.
must_try: Just show up — the music is the thing

name: Buddy Guy's Legends
description: Blues legend's own South Loop club. Buddy still plays his January residency. Decent Southern food.

name: Rosa's Lounge
description: Intimate Logan Square blues joint run by an Italian immigrant who fell in love with Chicago blues. Raw, authentic, no tourists.
must_try: Any weeknight show — small room, big sound

name: B.L.U.E.S.
description: Tiny Lincoln Park blues bar across from Kingston Mines. 100-capacity room where you're practically on stage with the band.
must_try: Any show — you're 5 feet from the artist

name: Green Mill Cocktail Lounge
description: Jazz club since 1907. Al Capone's booth still roped off. Sunday Uptown Poetry Slam is the longest-running in the country.
must_try: Sunday Poetry Slam, any weeknight jazz set

name: Jazz Showcase
description: South Loop jazz institution since 1947. Straight-ahead jazz in a proper listening room. All-ages matinees on Sundays.

name: Andy's Jazz Club
description: River North jazz club with early and late sets. More accessible/tourist-friendly than Green Mill but the music is serious.

name: Winter's Jazz Club
description: Intimate Streeterville jazz room. Chicago-style jazz in a 50-seat space. BYOB.
must_try: Any show — 50 seats means you're IN it

name: The Violet Hour
description: James Beard Award-winning cocktail bar. No sign — unmarked door in Wicker Park. Craft cocktails, speakeasy vibe.

name: Lost Lake
description: Top-tier tiki bar from the Violet Hour crew. Tropical cocktails with dead-serious technique. Avondale.

name: Three Dots and a Dash
description: Underground tiki bar beneath River North. Over-the-top tropical drinks in coconuts and skulls.

name: Kumiko
description: Japanese-inspired cocktail bar above Kikko in West Loop. Julia Momosé's cocktails are art. One of the best bars in America.

name: The Aviary
description: Grant Achatz's cocktail laboratory. Drinks served in ice spheres, presented like tasting-menu courses. The Office below is the speakeasy.
must_try: The kitchen table experience, then The Office downstairs

name: Billy Sunday
description: Logan Square cocktail bar named after a prohibition-era preacher. Amaro-focused, deep spirits knowledge.

name: Cindy's Rooftop
description: Chicago Athletic Association rooftop overlooking Millennium Park. The view is extraordinary. Get there early.
must_try: Cocktail at sunset overlooking The Bean

name: The Signature Lounge
address: 875 N Michigan Ave, 96th Floor, Chicago, IL 60611
description: 96th floor cocktails — free to enter (no observation deck fee). 360-degree skyline view. Come for drinks, skip the food.
must_try: Any cocktail — you're paying for the view

name: I|O Godfrey
description: River North rooftop bar and lounge. Heated in winter, open-air in summer. DJ sets on weekends.

name: Revolution Brewing
description: Largest independent brewery in Illinois. Logan Square brewpub with great food. Anti-Hero IPA is everywhere for a reason.

name: Half Acre Beer Company
description: Lincoln Square taproom and beer garden. Daisy Cutter is the house classic.

name: Goose Island Brewhouse
description: The original brewpub where Chicago craft beer started. Now AB InBev-owned but the Clybourn taproom still pours exclusive small-batch.

name: Dovetail Brewery
address: 1800 W Belle Plaine Ave, Chicago, IL 60613
description: Ravenswood lager brewery. Traditional German and Belgian styles. The Hefeweizen and Vienna Lager are exceptional.

name: Metropolitan Brewing
description: Avondale lager-focused brewery with a gorgeous riverfront taproom. German-style lagers only. Krankshaft is the flagship.

name: Hopleaf
description: Andersonville Belgian beer bar with one of the deepest beer lists in America. The mussels and frites are mandatory.
must_try: Mussels and frites, any Belgian ale on tap

name: Old Town Ale House
description: Old Town legend since 1958. Paintings of naked politicians on the walls. Cash only. Across from Second City.
must_try: Cheap beer and the art on the walls

name: The California Clipper
description: Humboldt Park vintage bar with a gorgeous 1940s curved bar. Live music, DJs, old-school charm.
must_try: Old fashioned at the curved bar

name: Simon's Tavern
description: Andersonville Swedish tavern since 1934. Glögg (hot mulled wine) in winter is a tradition. Neon sign is iconic.
must_try: Glögg in winter, cheap beer anytime

name: Nisei Lounge
description: Wrigleyville's oldest tavern (1951). Authentic, gritty counterpoint to the sports bar corridor. Cash only.

name: L&L Tavern
description: Lakeview East dive cherished for its unapologetically stark atmosphere and dark lore. Cash only.

name: Carol's Pub
description: Uptown honky-tonk dive with live country music. One of the last real country bars in Chicago. Beloved institution.

name: Maria's Packaged Goods
description: Bridgeport bar/liquor store hybrid. Amazing craft beer selection in a no-frills neighborhood institution. DJ nights.

name: Estelle's Cafe & Lounge
description: Wicker Park 4AM bar with late-night food. Tater tots at 3am. Industry hangout.

name: The Owl
description: Logan Square 4AM late-night lounge. Dark, moody, perfect for the 2am crowd that's not ready to stop.

name: Smartbar
description: Below Metro. Chicago house music institution since 1982. Where house music lives. Legendary DJs, no bottle service nonsense.
must_try: Late-night DJ set — this is where house was born

name: Spybar
description: River North underground dance club. Top-tier electronic music bookings in an intimate basement.

name: Murphy's Bleachers
description: THE Wrigley Field pregame bar. Right across from the bleacher entrance. Packed on game days, essential Cubs experience.

name: Second City
description: The most important comedy theater in America. Tina Fey, Bill Murray, Stephen Colbert started here. Mainstage and improv nightly.

name: iO Theater
description: Legendary improv theater. More experimental than Second City. Harold Night is a Chicago institution.

name: Zanies Comedy Night Club
description: Old Town standup comedy club. Touring national headliners in an intimate room. Two-drink minimum.

name: Intelligentsia Coffee
description: The Chicago third-wave coffee pioneer. Multiple locations. Meticulous roasting, beautiful spaces.

name: Metric Coffee
description: Fulton Market roastery and cafe. Beautiful industrial space. Best single-origin pours in the city.

name: Dark Matter Coffee
description: Ukrainian Village punk-rock coffee roaster. Bold blends, wild branding, great espresso. Multiple locations.
must_try: A Coffee Guy Fieri Would Drink blend

name: Sawada Coffee
description: West Loop latte art champion café. Military Latte (matcha + espresso) is the signature. Tiny, beautiful space.

name: Lost Larson
description: Andersonville Scandinavian bakery. Cardamom buns, croissants, rye bread. Will derail your morning plans.

name: Hoosier Mama Pie Company
description: East Village pie shop. Everything from scratch. The salted caramel apple and sugar cream pies are iconic.

name: Margie's Candies
description: Bucktown ice cream parlor since 1921. Giant sundaes in a clamshell dish, homemade hot fudge. Time capsule.

name: Rainbow Cone
description: Beverly institution since 1926. Five flavors stacked in one cone — chocolate, strawberry, Palmer House, pistachio, orange sherbet. Iconic.
must_try: The Rainbow Cone — all five flavors

name: Art Institute of Chicago
description: One of the greatest art museums on earth. 300,000+ works. Sunday on La Grande Jatte, Nighthawks, American Gothic — all here. Free select Thu evenings.

name: Field Museum
address: 1400 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
description: World-class natural history. SUE the T. rex, Máximo the Titanosaur, Egyptian tomb recreation. Free for IL residents every Wednesday.

name: Museum of Science and Industry
address: 5700 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60637
description: Largest science museum in the Western Hemisphere. WWII U-505 submarine, 40-foot tornado, coal mine ride. IL resident free days.

name: Shedd Aquarium
address: 1200 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
description: Lakefront aquarium with 32,000+ animals. Beluga whales headline. IL resident free days available.

name: Adler Planetarium
address: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
description: First planetarium in the Western Hemisphere. Sky shows, space artifacts. Best skyline photo spot from the lakefront steps.
must_try: Grainger Sky Theater, skyline photo from steps

name: National Museum of Mexican Art
description: Pilsen. Free always. 10,000+ works spanning 3,000 years of Mexican art and culture. Day of the Dead exhibit is extraordinary.
must_try: Permanent collection, Day of the Dead (Oct)

name: MCA Chicago
description: Museum of Contemporary Art. Bold exhibitions, great rooftop terrace, excellent gift shop. Streeterville.

name: Chicago History Museum
description: Lincoln Park. Chicago Fire diorama, Lincoln's deathbed, city history told neighborhood by neighborhood.
must_try: Great Chicago Fire exhibit, Chicago Room

name: Driehaus Museum
description: Gilded Age mansion museum. Tiffany glass, ornate interiors. Like stepping into 1890s Chicago wealth. Near Mag Mile.
must_try: The stained glass collection, period rooms

name: The Hand & The Eye
description: Opening April 2026. $50M, 35,000 sq ft immersive magic venue in a historic mansion. Secret passageways, world-class illusionists, Levy Restaurants dining. Tickets from $225.

name: Obama Presidential Center
description: Opening spring 2026 in historic Jackson Park. Community events, exhibits, workshops, presidential archives.

name: Willis Tower Skydeck
description: The Ledge — glass boxes 1,353 feet up. Four-state views on clear days.

name: 360 Chicago
description: 1,000-foot observation deck. TILT tilts you out over Michigan Ave. Sunset views are magical.

name: Millennium Park
description: Chicago's front yard. Cloud Gate (The Bean), Crown Fountain, Pritzker Pavilion, Lurie Garden. Free concerts all summer.
must_try: Bean photo, free concert at Pritzker Pavilion

name: Navy Pier
description: 50-acre entertainment complex. Centennial Wheel, Children's Museum, boat tours. Touristy but the Ferris wheel views are real.
must_try: Centennial Wheel at sunset, summer fireworks (Wed & Sat)

name: Chicago Architecture Center River Cruise
description: The single best tour in Chicago. 90-minute docent-narrated cruise through the river canyon. Consistently #1 US boat tour.

name: Garfield Park Conservatory
address: 300 N Central Park Ave, Chicago, IL 60624
description: One of the largest conservatories in the nation. Tropical rooms, desert house, fern room. Free always.

name: Goodman Theatre
description: Chicago's flagship nonprofit theater. World premieres, classic revivals. Two stages in the Loop.

name: Steppenwolf Theatre
description: Founded by Gary Sinise, John Malkovich, and ensemble. Bold, raw, ensemble-driven theater. New state-of-the-art building.

name: Lincoln Park Zoo
description: Free zoo in Lincoln Park. Lions, gorillas, penguins, nature boardwalk. One of the last free major zoos in America.

name: North Avenue Beach
address: 1600 N DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60614
description: The main beach scene. Steamship-shaped beach house, volleyball, kayaks, full skyline backdrop.

name: Oak Street Beach
address: 1000 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60611
description: Gold Coast beach steps from the Mag Mile. More intimate than North Ave. Urban beach at its finest.
must_try: Morning swim with the skyline behind you

name: Montrose Beach
address: 4400 N DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60640
description: Uptown beach with a dog beach section. More local, less tourist. Great bird sanctuary adjacent.
must_try: Dog beach, Montrose Point bird sanctuary

name: Lakefront Trail
description: 18-mile paved path. Runners, bikers, walkers. Best urban trail in America.
must_try: Bike from Navy Pier to Museum Campus

name: The 606 / Bloomingdale Trail
address: Walsh Park to Ridgeway Trailhead, Chicago, IL
description: 2.7-mile elevated trail on a former rail line. Connects Bucktown, Wicker Park, Humboldt Park, Logan Square. Chicago's High Line.
must_try: Walk or bike the full 2.7 miles at sunset

name: Maggie Daley Park
description: Next to Millennium Park. Rock climbing wall, skating ribbon (winter), play gardens. Design-forward.
must_try: Skating Ribbon in winter, climbing wall in summer

name: Urban Kayaks
description: Kayak or paddleboard the Chicago River through downtown. Architecture views from water level.

name: Reckless Records
description: The definitive Chicago record store. Extensive new and used vinyl. Three locations — Wicker Park is the flagship.

name: Dusty Groove
description: Globally renowned for soul, funk, jazz, and rare international vinyl. West Town. Mail-order legend with a physical shop.
must_try: Rare jazz and funk vinyl section

name: Myopic Books
description: Three floors of labyrinthine used books in Wicker Park. A neighborhood institution. Get lost in here.

name: Seminary Co-op Bookstores
description: Hyde Park. Renowned academic bookstore serving the U of C community. One of the great bookstores in America.
must_try: Browse the philosophy and history sections

name: Quimby's Bookstore
description: Wicker Park paradise for zines, indie comics, and underground literature. Weird and wonderful.
hours: Mon-Thu noon-9pm, Fri-Sat noon-10pm, Sun noon-7pm

name: Women & Children First
description: Legendary feminist bookstore in Andersonville since 1979. Author events, strong community focus.
must_try: Author event calendar, curated staff picks

name: Magnificent Mile
address: N Michigan Ave, Chicago River to Oak St
description: 13 blocks of luxury retail. Apple, Nordstrom, Burberry, Louis Vuitton. The flagship shopping corridor.
must_try: Window shopping from the river to Oak Street Beach

name: Green City Market
description: Chicago's premier outdoor farmers market. Local produce, artisan foods, chef demos. Saturday ritual for foodies.

name: AIRE Ancient Baths
description: Roman-style thermal baths in a restored 1902 factory. Multiple temperature pools, salt bath, steam room, candlelight. Off-peak weekday sessions $15-20 less.

name: King Spa & Sauna
description: 24-hour Korean spa in suburban Niles. $75 entry. Multiple saunas (base rock, pyramid, fire), food court with bibimbap, traditional body scrubs.

name: The Langham Chicago
description: #3 hotel in the US (2026). Mies van der Rohe building, river views, Chuan Spa, afternoon tea. $400-800+/night.

name: The Peninsula Chicago
description: Magnificent Mile luxury. Exceptional spa, rooftop terrace, white-glove service. $500-900+/night.

name: Chicago Athletic Association
description: Restored 1890s sporting club overlooking Millennium Park. Cindy's Rooftop, the Drawing Room, game room. $250-500/night.
must_try: Drinks at Cindy's Rooftop, Drawing Room cocktails

name: The Hoxton Chicago
description: Fulton Market lifestyle hotel. Stylish rooms, great lobby bar, walking distance to Restaurant Row. $200-400/night.

name: The Robey
description: Art Deco tower at the Wicker Park/Bucktown/Ukrainian Village intersection. Rooftop bar, neighborhood character. $150-300/night.

name: Palmer House Hilton
description: Historic Loop hotel since 1871. The painted lobby ceiling alone is worth a visit. Central to everything. $150-350/night.

name: HI Chicago Hostel
description: Clean, social hostel in the Loop. Dorms from $35-60/night. Walking distance to Museum Campus and Grant Park.

name: Bally's Chicago Casino & Hotel
description: Opening late 2026/early 2027. $1.7B riverfront complex. 500 rooms, 3,300 slots, 170 tables, 3,000-seat theater, riverwalk. Temp casino operating at Medinah Temple now.

name: Wrigley Field
description: The Friendly Confines. Built 1914. Ivy, marquee, rooftop bars. Wrigleyville on game day is an experience even if you hate baseball.
must_try: Bleacher seats, pregame at Murphy's Bleachers

name: Soldier Field
description: Home of the Bears. Lakefront stadium with Museum Campus views. Tailgating culture is as important as the game.

name: United Center
description: Home of the Bulls and Blackhawks. MJ statue. 2026 WNBA All-Star Game host. Major concert venue.

name: Guaranteed Rate Field
description: Home of the White Sox. Bridgeport/Armour Square. Less touristy than Wrigley, cheaper tickets, better sight lines.
must_try: Elote helmet nachos, craft beer garden

name: Walgreens (Michigan Ave 24hr)
description: 24-hour pharmacy on the Magnificent Mile. Everything a tourist needs at 2am.

name: Whole Foods (Gold Coast)
description: Best-stocked downtown grocery. Hot bar, prepared foods, rental stocking.

name: Michigan Avenue Primary Care & Immediate Care
description: Walk-in urgent care directly in the Loop. No appointment needed.

name: Bounce Luggage Storage
